latentclasscausal: causal inference for latent class models

latentclasscausal-package.Rd

latentclasscausal answers causal questions about latent classes (from latentmixtures::lca() or latentmixtures::lpa() models):

Details

  1. Does a treatment change latent class membership? intervene_membership() estimates \(\Delta_k = P(C(1) = k) - P(C(0) = k)\) with an augmented inverse probability weighting estimator that uses bias-corrected (BCH) pseudo-outcomes, cross-fitting and influence-function standard errors that include the measurement model; extensions intervene_subgroup(), intervene_membership_sensitivity(), intervene_dif().

  2. Interventions on exposures that form latent classes (e.g. childhood adversities): the effect on membership in a latent class outcome (intervene_latent_outcome()), effects within each latent class of the exposures (intervene_within()), sensitivity to a direct effect of the latent class (intervene_latent_sensitivity()), adjustment for the latent pattern of the other exposures (intervene_effect(adjust = "classes")) and the classification of post-intervention profiles (intervene_shares(), descriptive).

These are built on intervene_effect(): static (setto()), stochastic (shift()) and targeted (subgroup()) interventions on binary exposures with the parametric g-formula, IPTW, AIPW or TMLE, which can also be used on their own.

Results have print(), tidy(), glance(), coef() and nobs() methods and can be tabulated with causal_table() or lm_table() and plotted with autoplot() (autoplot.lcc_result()) or causal_plot(). The assumptions of both methods are set out in their help pages and in vignette("latentclasscausal").

Which estimators are established in the literature, which adapt a published method, and which are the package's own (experimental) constructions is tabulated, with the supporting references, in the Method status section of the home page of the LatentClassCausal.jl documentation (docs/src/index.md of the Julia package).

Architecture

latentclasscausal is an R front end to the Julia package LatentClassCausal.jl, called through JuliaConnectoR. It shares the Julia process managed by latentmixtures: the first call starts it if needed (through latentmixtures::lm_start(), with JULIA_NUM_THREADS or one thread per core), then loads LatentClassCausal.jl and this package's bridge module (inst/julia/bridge.jl) into the same process, so fitted measurement models are passed to Julia by reference without copying. When the session is ended or restarted (latentmixtures::lm_end()), the bridge is reloaded on the next call; models fitted in an earlier session must be refitted. Install the Julia packages with latentmixtures::install_julia_packages() (argument causal_url or causal_path).

Options

options(latentclasscausal.ascii = TRUE) prints ASCII instead of UTF-8 symbols.
